- A PLY mesh file containing vertex positions (float32) and face indices (int32), with vertex colors.

- Project to pixel coordinates: $v_{image} = (K @ v_{cam})^T$.
- Sample colors from the image at projected pixel coordinates using bilinear interpolation (e.g., `cv2.remap`).
- Predict occlusion: Construct rays from camera origin to vertices.
Set near bound to dataset bounds minimum and far bound to vertex depth.
- Accumulate weighted colors: $v_{color\_sum} += colors \times non\_occluded$.
It computes the median depth $\hat{z}_{i,p,50}$ as the first index where accumulated transmittance $T_k > 50/100$.
- **Time Complexity:** Dominated by the NeRF queries for density ($O(N_{grid}^3)$) and color fusion ($O(N_{vertices} \times N_{views} \times N_{samples})$).
The chunking strategy mitigates memory usage but increases I/O overhead.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the density grid ($N_{grid}^3$) and intermediate ray marching results.
